mission: Maintain endogenous Coenzyme Q synthesis, maturation and pool availability to support mitochondrial electron transfer and cellular redox functions.
placement: No existing BRS4 PM owns endogenous CoQ production/maturation/distribution; FM1 supports cellular bioenergetic carrier pools. Existing PM1 owns downstream electron transfer.

dietary_admissions.operation: Maintain endogenous Coenzyme Q synthesis, maturation and pool availability to support mitochondrial electron transfer and cellular redox functions.
dietary_admissions.assessment_limitations: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established. Endogenous phenylalanine conversion is an alternative source; the full human intervening enzyme sequence remains incompletely assigned.

functional_dependency.statement: Tyrosine supplies quinone-head carbon through the HPDL-associated 4-HMA/4-HB pathway.

dietary_supply.statement: Existing canonical food composition records establish dietary provision of this named nutrient, independently of its CoQ role.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Reused existing amino-acid, riboflavin and iron composition records with original food-state and measurement provenance. exercise.input: Twelve-week supervised endurance and resistance training
exercise.biological_role: In the studied statin-user and non-user cohort, twelve weeks of combined endurance and resistance training was associated with a modest increase in total CoQ10 per gram of wet skeletal muscle.
exercise.evidence_limitation: No inactive comparison, some missing biopsies, sex/statin differences and one cohort. Concentration per wet mass is not mitochondrial-normalised concentration, synthesis rate, turnover, redistribution or redox state. CoQ change was not shown to mediate function.

moa.description: Training may alter synthesis, turnover, fibre composition or intracellular distribution; these alternatives were not isolated.
moa.evidenceQualification: No measured biosynthetic flux, mitochondrial-normalised CoQ or redox adaptation.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: In the studied statin-user and non-user cohort, twelve weeks of combined endurance and resistance training was associated with a modest increase in total CoQ10 per gram of wet skeletal muscle.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Directly measures total muscle CoQ concentration, within pool availability, without identifying its cause.

limitations.text: No inactive control and one reused cohort.
Wet-muscle concentration, not mitochondrial-normalised concentration or synthetic flux.
Parent trial ATP-production capacity and peak oxygen uptake did not change detectably.

nonadmissions.disposition: Upstream systemic tyrosine contribution acknowledged; no separate duplicate admission without quantified PM-specific contribution.
Genotype-specific precursor bypass is research/clinical context, not an ordinary dietary admission.
Food occurrence retained; general muscle target engagement not established by plasma exposure. No general Type B admission.
Endogenous pathway participants; no direct dietary requirement inferred.
Reconstituted assay roles noted; further human-specific dependency appraisal required before expanding dietary admissions.
Defer causal intervention admission; observed cohort adaptation retained as SF4 and candidate six-atom record.

kc: None created; no coherent shared pool established merely by multiple pathway cofactors.
